whyItIsAProblem: governingSources[4] is the COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md entry, so 'Live digest only at reMeasurementAtV4' is a statement about where the live COORD digest is found. reMeasurementAtV4.livePinsNamedPropertyOnly['docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md'] is d210f103fc32a36e2220acd4c9bab8c7db1102370ba299c9989e9f54f9642166. Live COORD measures cda503800913e5a12442f4074b2836505b85f1694cba86a1b38a785f7d6040c2. The two sentences cannot both be true.

This is not inherited damage. At signed-index-trust-contract.v9 the redirect was stale but internally consistent: nothing in v9 disclaimed reMeasurementAtV4, so the artifact's position was simply that d210f103... was live COORD, and CLAUDE-V9-M1 charged that staleness against the live file. signed-index-trust-contract.v10 fixes the fact and creates the contradiction, by adding a field that says reMeasurementAtV4's pins are not live while leaving the pointer aimed at them.

It is the same defect class CLAUDE-V9-S3 named one lineage step earlier - a second pin inside one artifact still labelled live after the artifact re-pins the real one - applied to COORD instead of file 08. signed-index-trust-contract.v10 repaired the file-08 instance cleanly and left the COORD instance standing. Two of the artifact's three COORD digests are now reachable through a sentence that calls one of them live.

The remedy is already demonstrated inside the same object. governingSources[4].role was rewritten and now reads 'D-293 Decision 6 is not this field. Live COORD for D-293 is decisionCarriedVerbatim. Live COORD is not this field.' The standing field sitting immediately beside it still points somewhere else. The author touched one of the two fields on this object and stopped.

Concrete consequence: a reader looking for the live COORD digest for anything other than D-293 - the D-002 G08 scope, the DR-110 repair deferral or the D-056 T2-02 sentence that governingSources[4].role names - follows standing to reMeasurementAtV4 and lands on a digest the artifact itself has just declared not live, with no third pin to fall back on. whyItIsAProblem: The block heading names a lineage step. honestyRepairsFromVK records what version K+1 repaired in response to the reviews of version K: honestyRepairsFromV1 carries SITCV1-*, honestyRepairsFromV7 carries CLAUDE-V7-ADV-1 / CODEX-V7-S1, and so on. Filing CLAUDE-V9-S2 in honestyRepairsFromV8 asserts by the block's own semantics that it was a v8-to-v9 repair. It cannot have been: CLAUDE-V9-S2 is a finding raised against signed-index-trust-contract.v9, and the text v10 deletes from [0] and [1] is precisely the wording that finding was raised against.

The same two repairs are now filed twice, under two different lineage steps. CLAUDE-V9-S2 appears at honestyRepairsFromV8[2] and again at honestyRepairsFromV9[2]; CLAUDE-V9-M1 is claimed at honestyRepairsFromV8[0] and recorded at honestyRepairsFromV9[0]. A later successor reading the blocks in order sees one finding landing at two steps.

This lineage has never done it before. I loaded all ten artifacts and compared each honestyRepairsFromVK block across every version that carries it. honestyRepairsFromV1 (introduced v2), V2 (v3), V3 (v4), V4 (v5), V5 (v6), V6 (v7) and V7 (v8) are byte-identical in every later version. honestyRepairsFromV8, introduced at v9, is mutated at v10. That is the first mutation in nine successors.

The lineage states the norm in its own text, and signed-index-trust-contract.v10 still carries it. honestyRepairsFromV2[3]: 'CLAUDE-V2-ADV-2: correction recorded here, not by mutating honestyRepairsFromV1: the v2 one-line B1 summary overstated from-sets; v3 names the actual from-sets and the monotonic stay-ACCEPT cases.' That is the same situation - a predecessor's one-line summary described its own work inaccurately - and the recorded remedy is to correct it in the current block and leave the predecessor's block alone. v10 does both: it writes the correct record in honestyRepairsFromV9 and also rewrites honestyRepairsFromV8.

basedOn.method still says only 'honestyRepairsFromV1 through honestyRepairsFromV6 are historical.' That sentence has been carried unchanged since signed-index-trust-contract.v8, where it was correct because V7 was then the current block. At v10 the current block is V9, so V7 and V8 are both historical and neither is declared so - and V8 is then the one that gets rewritten. The declaration and the act point in opposite directions.

What is lost is the predecessor's own account of itself. A reader of v10 can no longer see from the artifact that v9 described the residual as 'Residual wording of the refusal (plain refuse versus preview refuse)'. The correction survives - honestyRepairsFromV8[2] says 'This is not a residual of message wording' and honestyRepairsFromV9[2] says 'not as message wording' - but the thing being corrected has been deleted from the record, so the correction no longer has a visible referent inside the artifact. I record that no statement in the rewritten block is false, and that the change is inside a rostered path and therefore declared rather than silent. The charge is to the honesty apparatus, not to the facts.
